texts: If the TAPVC is unobstructed, presentation may be delayed: B.
With a free path back to the heart, the infant has a large left-to-right shunt and only mild cyanosis, and may present weeks or months later with breathlessness and poor growth.
Obstructed TAPVC, typically the infracardiac form, presents in the first hours with severe cyanosis and pulmonary oedema and is a surgical emergency.
A large coronary sinus belongs to the cardiac form, and echo shows a large right heart and small left-sided chambers.
In the picture, the baby with the free-flowing tap plays for weeks, while the baby with the pinched tap is blue and soggy at birth.
Memory hook: a free tap, a late visit; a pinched tap, an emergency.
